newsitem.title: FRANCE: EU scraps weekly wheat tax tenders - ONIC.
newsitem.headline: EU scraps weekly wheat tax tenders - ONIC.

text.p: The European Union on Thursday voted a regulation that will prevent traders from submitting bids to export free-market soft wheat with a tax through its weekly grain tender system, France's grain office ONIC said.

Since last December traders have been able to submit bids to export EU soft wheat with taxes or/and subsidies at the weekly tenders. The EU grain panel in turn could grant exports with taxes or/and refunds.
Up to now the Commission has been reluctant to sell wheat with refunds apart from limited tonnages granted to African, Caribbean and Pacific nations under a special tender.
EU officials had said the Commission was unlikely to restore wheat subsidies as long as some traders were willing to pay a tax to export EU wheat.
Earlier traders reported the Commission granted exports of 4,500 tonnes of free-market soft wheat at a minimum tax of 0.05 Ecus per tonne, to non-EU countries.
On Thursday the EU grain panel also scrapped the daily export tax applying to the daily soft wheat and durum wheat export channels, replacing it with a zero refund. --Paris newsroom +331 4221 5432
